title: Consumer lag alert copied as a raw message count with no freshness SLO behind it
code_snippet:
# alerting rule inherited from another team's runbook
- alert: ConsumerLagHigh
  expr: kafka_consumergroup_lag > 10000
  for: 5m
  labels: {severity: page}
  annotations:
    summary: "Consumer lag high"
expected_feedback: Standard: the threshold is a copied constant, not a derived one, and at this throughput it is close to meaningless. 10 000 messages is four seconds of backlog for a 2 500/s consumer and over four minutes for this one at 40/s per partition — the same rule pages instantly on one service and never on another. Alert on time-to-drain instead: lag_seconds is roughly records_lag_max / records_consumed_rate, and the threshold comes from the freshness the downstream consumer has committed to. If no freshness SLO exists, that absence is the actual finding; a number invented mid-incident is not a substitute. Add a trend alert as well — steadily rising lag_seconds at any absolute value means consumption is structurally slower than production and will breach retention eventually, which a fixed ceiling only catches once it is nearly too late. Set the `for:` duration longer than one deploy/rebalance cycle so a rolling restart does not page anyone.
violated_rule: Consumer lag monitoring with an alert threshold defined
checklist_anchor: a copied message count is meaningless across workloads
